steps.name: Mother
steps.text: You've gotten so good at the piano!

steps.name: Sakiko Togawa
steps.text: D-Do you think so?

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: I know better than anyone how much you've changed. I'm your mother, after all.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: I can hear it all—how hard you've been working... I know your job must be so hectic, and yet you've kept up with your piano practice.

steps.name: Sakiko Togawa
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: It seems you've gone through quite a lot out there...

steps.name: Father
steps.text: Hate to disturb you two while you're practicing! Supper's ready?

steps.name: Sakiko Togawa
steps.text: Mm—this is wonderful!

steps.name: Father
steps.text: What do you think? My cooking's really improved, eh?

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: You don't know the half of it, Sakiko... He had me taste-test so much in order to finally get to this point.

steps.name: Father
steps.text: Hurry and give this salad a try, hm?

steps.name: Sakiko Togawa
steps.text: Mmh! Delicious!

steps.name: Father
steps.text: I've made a lot of minor adjustments so it's more to your liking! Not half bad, eh?

steps.name: Father
steps.text: And there's plenty more dishes you love on the way!

steps.name: Sakiko Togawa
steps.text: Yep!

steps.name: Sakiko Togawa
steps.text: Ngh... Ugh...

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Sakiko? Sakiko!

steps.name: Father
steps.text: Wh-What's wrong?

steps.name: Sakiko Togawa
steps.text: I think—I've had a little too much to eat...

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Are you feeling better now...?

steps.name: Father
steps.text: Sorry, I think I overdid it a little...

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Honestly, your father never changes...

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: But that's his style, I suppose. Honestly, most times it's quite adorable of him.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: You'll forgive him, won't you?

a.text: When the man who shares his face has broken my heart countless times?

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: He really loves you, you know.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: And so do I.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: I really love the both of you.

steps.name: Sakiko Togawa
steps.text: Mother, where is this coming from...?

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: I've been going through our photo albums more and more while you were away.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: I started from when you were born... then when you were one, then two, then three...

steps.name: Sakiko Togawa
steps.text: My childhood memory nearly failed me...

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Maybe. But there's nothing more important, nothing more special to a parent than their child.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: When you were born, your palm wasn't even half as big as mine.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: But look at you now. Yours is even a little bigger.
Sakiko's mother takes her hand and brings their palms together.
For some reason beyond herself, Sakiko grasps her mother's hand and locks fingers with hers.

steps.name: Sakiko Togawa
steps.text: Mother, your hand is so warm...

a.text: Was this how warm her palm is?
Is this all real? Is everything I'm enjoying right now rational, reasonable?
How can it be this warm, and yet this heartrending?

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: That's right. I'm right here.

steps.name: Sakiko Togawa
steps.text: Mother...

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Go on. You can cry all you want. I always comforted you like this when you cried.

steps.name: Sakiko Togawa
steps.text: Huh? Was I... really such a crybaby?

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: When you were very, veeery little. Oh, you would make the biggest fuss over a single sweet.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: You may be a strong young woman now, but you were a big crybaby back then.

steps.name: Sakiko Togawa
steps.text: R-Really? I don't remember at all...

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: *giggle* Your mother would never lie to you.

steps.name: Sakiko Togawa
steps.text: Then... Do you remember my high school entrance ceremony?

a.text: During my last year of middle school, my mother died of illness.
Even if they're nonexistent memories, even if they're things that never happened.
But right now, all I want is the most beautiful answers I can get.
I want to convince myself, to create the most wonderful memories, to believe in the sweetest dream I can.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Of course. I remember you in your school uniform. Our whole family took a photo together at the school gate.

steps.name: Sakiko Togawa
steps.text: Yes, that sounds right... Oh, that does bring me back.

steps.name: Sakiko Togawa
steps.text: What else have we done together? Mother... I want you to tell me. Tell me about all the memories we share.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Sakiko, just how long have you been away from home? Aren't you the clingy one today?

steps.name: Sakiko Togawa
steps.text: Home...

a.text: When did the word 'home' start sounding so foreign to me?

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Hmm... Well, if you want, I'll reminisce a little more.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Now where should I begin?

steps.name: Sakiko Togawa
steps.text: Let's start from when I was born. I want to hear it all.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Okay, then we'll start from the day you were born...
And so, down the country path, at a leisurely pace, Sakiko and her mother walk side-by-side, and it feels as if they could walk forever.
Just like that sweet, beautiful stretch of time they shared back when it all began. Unhurried and without end.
Their hands, the umbilical cord that connected them in the very beginning.
Sakiko—

steps.name: Vigna
steps.text: You found your way home!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: Miss Vigna, this carriage seems to be out of order. Now let me down!

steps.name: Vigna
steps.text: Let's see... W—Wait, these controls aren't like what I learned at Rhodes Island!

steps.name: Vigna
steps.text: Oh, crap, crap, crap, we can't stop!

steps.name: Iris
steps.text: We're going to crash!

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Sakiko, out of the way—!
